title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: perspectiveR provides R interface FINOS Perspective library, high-performance WebAssembly-powered data visualization engine. offers interactive pivot tables, cross-tabulations, multiple chart types run entirely browser.

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: simplest usage pass data frame directly: opens fully interactive viewer settings panel can: Drag columns /view Switch chart types (datagrid, bar, line, scatter, heatmap, etc.) Add group-(row pivot) split-(column pivot) dimensions Create filters, sort, change aggregations Write computed expressions
code: library(perspectiveR) perspective(mtcars)

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: can set initial configuration programmatically: Users can still modify view interactively even initial configuration.
code: perspective(mtcars,   group_by = "cyl",   columns = c("mpg", "hp", "wt"),   plugin = "Y Bar",   theme = "Pro Dark" )

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: "Datagrid" — interactive data grid (default) "Y Bar" / "X Bar" — vertical / horizontal bar charts "Y Line" — line chart "X/Y Line" — line chart explicit X axis "Y Area" — area chart "Y Scatter" / "XY Scatter" — scatter plots "Treemap" — treemap "Sunburst" — sunburst chart "Heatmap" — heatmap

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
code: perspective(iris,   filter = list(c("Species", "==", "setosa")),   sort = list(c("Sepal.Length", "desc")) )

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
code: perspective(mtcars,   expressions = c('"hp" / "wt"'),   columns = c("mpg", "hp", "wt", '"hp" / "wt"') )

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: datasets 100k+ rows, use Arrow IPC serialization better performance:
code: # Requires the arrow package big_data <- data.frame(   x = rnorm(100000),   y = rnorm(100000),   group = sample(letters, 100000, replace = TRUE) ) perspective(big_data, use_arrow = TRUE)

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: perspectiveR includes full Shiny support proxy interface streaming updates:
code: library(shiny)  ui <- fluidPage(   perspectiveOutput("viewer", height = "600px"),   actionButton("add", "Add Data") )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$viewer <- renderPerspective({     perspective(mtcars, plugin = "Y Bar", group_by = "cyl")   })    observeEvent(input$add, {     proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer")     new_data <- mtcars[sample(nrow(mtcars), 5), ]     psp_update(proxy, new_data)   })    # Capture user's interactive config changes   observeEvent(input$viewer_config, {     message("User changed config: ", str(input$viewer_config))   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: psp_update(proxy, data) — append new rows (upserts table index) psp_replace(proxy, data) — replace data psp_clear(proxy) — clear rows psp_restore(proxy, config) — apply config psp_reset(proxy) — reset defaults psp_remove(proxy, keys) — remove rows primary key (indexed tables ) psp_export(proxy, format) — export data JSON, CSV, columns, Arrow (supports windowed export) psp_save(proxy) — retrieve current viewer state psp_on_update(proxy, enable) — subscribe/unsubscribe data change events psp_schema(proxy) — get table schema (column names types) psp_size(proxy) — get table row count psp_columns(proxy) — get table column names psp_validate_expressions(proxy, expressions) — validate expression strings

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: using multiple filters, can control combined using filter_op: default "" (filters must match). Set filter_op = "" match rows satisfy filter.
code: # Match rows where Species is "setosa" OR Sepal.Length > 6 perspective(iris,   filter = list(     c("Species", "==", "setosa"),     c("Sepal.Length", ">", "6")   ),   filter_op = "or" )

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Use limit parameter create rolling-window table automatically drops oldest rows new rows added beyond limit: Note limit index mutually exclusive.
code: # Keep only the last 100 rows perspective(streaming_data, limit = 100)

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Use index parameter create keyed table. index set, psp_update() performs upserts—rows matching keys updated instead appended—psp_remove() can delete rows key.
code: # Create an indexed table keyed on "cyl" perspective(mtcars, index = "cyl", plugin = "Datagrid")  # In a Shiny server: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer") psp_update(proxy, updated_rows)   # upserts by "cyl" psp_remove(proxy, keys = c(4, 8)) # remove rows where cyl == 4 or 8

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Request current view’s data browser: Supported formats: "json", "csv", "columns", "arrow" (base64-encoded).
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer") psp_export(proxy, format = "csv")  # Result arrives asynchronously: observeEvent(input$viewer_export, {   cat("Format:", input$viewer_export$format, "\n")   cat("Data:", input$viewer_export$data, "\n") })

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Retrieve current viewer configuration restore later:
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer")  # Save current state psp_save(proxy) observeEvent(input$viewer_state, {   saved <- input$viewer_state   # Later, restore it:   psp_restore(proxy, saved) })

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Subscribe table data changes react data updated:
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer") psp_on_update(proxy, enable = TRUE)  observeEvent(input$viewer_update, {   info <- input$viewer_update   message("Update at ", info$timestamp, " from ", info$source) })  # To unsubscribe: psp_on_update(proxy, enable = FALSE)

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Query table schema, size, column names:
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer")  # Get column types psp_schema(proxy) observeEvent(input$viewer_schema, {   str(input$viewer_schema)  # list(col1 = "float", col2 = "string", ...) })  # Get row count psp_size(proxy) observeEvent(input$viewer_size, {   message("Table has ", input$viewer_size, " rows") })  # Get column names psp_columns(proxy) observeEvent(input$viewer_columns, {   message("Columns: ", paste(input$viewer_columns, collapse = ", ")) })

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Export subset rows/columns specifying window:
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer")  # Export only the first 50 rows psp_export(proxy, format = "json", start_row = 0, end_row = 50)  # Export rows 100-200, columns 0-3 psp_export(proxy, format = "csv",   start_row = 100, end_row = 200,   start_col = 0, end_col = 3 )

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Check whether expression strings valid applying :
code: proxy <- perspectiveProxy(session, "viewer") psp_validate_expressions(proxy, c('"hp" / "wt"', '"invalid_col" + 1'))  observeEvent(input$viewer_validate_expressions, {   result <- input$viewer_validate_expressions   # Contains validation info for each expression   str(result) })

title: Introduction to perspectiveR
text: Set visual theme theme parameter: Available themes: "Pro Light" (default), "Pro Dark", "Monokai", "Solarized Light", "Solarized Dark", "Vaporwave", "Dracula", "Gruvbox", "Gruvbox Dark".
code: perspective(mtcars, theme = "Pro Dark") perspective(mtcars, theme = "Dracula") perspective(mtcars, theme = "Gruvbox Dark")

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: Drag--drop plotting useful quick EDA: glance data shaped, spot outliers. also works well need share playground someone less technical different stack — browser modern IDEs render HTML just fine. R already good options . GWalkR positions Tableau-like drag--drop interface. esquisse lets build ggplots interactively. great GUI-first workflow. perspectiveR something bit different. ’s htmlwidgets binding FINOS Perspective, WebAssembly data engine originally built financial dashboards. focus pivot tables live grouping, splitting, filtering, multiple chart types — running client-side. also pairs well Shiny: data updates stream without re-rendering chart, makes smooth experience.
code: # Stable release install.packages("perspectiveR")  # Development version --- new features and bug fixes land here first remotes::install_github("EydlinIlya/perspectiveR") library(perspectiveR)

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: ’s . Take look settings panel (top-right). can drag columns Group , Split , add filters, change sort order, switch 11 chart types, pick theme. R code sets starting point — viewer play .
code: # adjust height to taste perspective(mtcars, height = "700px")

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: Things get interesting layer group_by, split_by, filters, aggregates: Months one axis, days , temperature color intensity. cold May 1973. ’re American might want Celsius — click New Column button (plus icon next column list) paste expression: swap original Temp column new one columns panel.
code: aq <- airquality aq$Month <- sprintf("%02d-%s", aq$Month, month.abb[aq$Month])  perspective(   aq,   plugin = "Heatmap",   group_by = "Month",   split_by = "Day",   columns = "Temp",   aggregates = list(Temp = "avg"),   title = "NYC Daily Temperatures, 1973",   theme = "Solarized Dark",   height = "700px" ) // Temp in Celsius ("Temp" - 32) * 5 / 9

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: Hadley Wickham famously doesn’t like pie charts. ’re Hadley Wickham, ’s sunburst: Inner ring region, outer ring division, slice size population. Vaporwave theme ’re committing crimes ggplot2 orthodoxy might well go . Try switching Treemap plugin dropdown rectangular version, pick Pro Light Pro Dark theme classic look.
code: states <- as.data.frame(state.x77) states$Region <- state.region states$Division <- state.division  perspective(   states,   plugin = "Sunburst",   group_by = c("Region", "Division"),   columns = "Population",   aggregates = list(Population = "sum"),   title = "US Population by Region & Division",   theme = "Vaporwave",   height = "700px" )

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: examples work Quarto, R Markdown, RStudio Viewer. perspectiveR also Shiny proxy interface — can stream rows viewer without re-rendering, listen click select events, save restore user configurations:
code: # Streaming stock market data with a rolling window perspectiveR::run_example("shiny-basic")  # Editable CRUD table perspectiveR::run_example("crud-table")

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Charts from R
text: next release add WebSocket support. Right now data flows R browser via htmlwidgets’ JSON serialization, works fine means entire dataset pass R’s session memory. Perspective natively speaks WebSocket — connecting directly unlock proper big-data streaming: browser talks straight Perspective server, R stays loop orchestration without bottlenecking data path.

text: Summarize data grouping rows splitting columns, custom aggregates:
code: # Average horsepower by cylinders and transmission type perspective(mtcars,   columns    = c("hp", "mpg", "wt"),   group_by   = "cyl",   split_by   = "am",   aggregates = list(hp = "avg", mpg = "avg", wt = "sum"),   plugin     = "Datagrid" )

code: # Sort airquality by Ozone descending, then Temp ascending perspective(airquality,   sort   = list(c("Ozone", "desc"), c("Temp", "asc")),   filter = list(c("Ozone", "is not null")) )

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Visualizations with Perspective
text: Combine filters "" (default) "":
code: # Cars that are either very efficient OR very powerful perspective(mtcars,   columns   = c("mpg", "hp", "cyl", "wt"),   filter    = list(c("mpg", ">", 30), c("hp", ">", 200)),   filter_op = "or",   sort      = list(c("mpg", "desc")) )

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Visualizations with Perspective
text: Create derived columns using Perspective’s expression language:
code: # Compute power-to-weight ratio and bin it perspective(mtcars,   expressions = c(     '"hp_per_ton" = "hp" / ("wt" * 1000)',     '"efficiency" = if ("mpg" > 25) { "high" } else { "low" }'   ),   columns  = c("hp", "wt", "mpg", "hp_per_ton", "efficiency"),   group_by = "efficiency",   plugin   = "Y Bar" )

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Visualizations with Perspective
text: Render 3D torus entirely Perspective’s expression engine — parametric angles come R, geometry shading math runs WebAssembly (hat-tip classic donut.c): Add streaming rotation Shiny — see run_example("spinning-donut").
code: # 3D donut — geometry computed in Perspective's expression engine torus <- expand.grid(   u = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80),   v = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80) )  perspective(torus,   expressions = c(     '"x" = (2 + cos("v")) * cos("u")',     '"y" = (2 + cos("v")) * sin("u")',     '"shade" = cos("v") * sin("u") + sin("v")'   ),   columns  = c("x", "y", "shade"),   plugin   = "XY Scatter",   theme    = "Pro Dark",   settings = FALSE,   title    = "Donut" )

title: Interactive Pivot Tables and Visualizations with Perspective
text: Perspective supports wide range chart types:
code: # Line chart — time series perspective(EuStockMarkets,   plugin = "Y Line",   title  = "European Stock Indices" )  # Heatmap — correlation-style view perspective(mtcars,   group_by = "cyl",   split_by = "gear",   columns  = c("mpg", "hp", "wt"),   plugin   = "Heatmap" )  # Sunburst — hierarchical breakdown perspective(mtcars,   group_by = c("cyl", "gear", "am"),   columns  = "mpg",   plugin   = "Sunburst" )

what: Create a Perspective Interactive Viewer — perspective
title: Create a Perspective Interactive Viewer — perspective
text: Creates interactive pivot table visualization widget powered FINOS Perspective library. viewer provides self-service UI users can interactively change chart types, group/split/filter/sort data, create computed columns, configure aggregations.

title: Create a Perspective Interactive Viewer — perspective
code: perspective(   data,   columns = NULL,   group_by = NULL,   split_by = NULL,   sort = NULL,   filter = NULL,   filter_op = NULL,   expressions = NULL,   aggregates = NULL,   plugin = NULL,   plugin_config = NULL,   theme = "Pro Light",   settings = TRUE,   title = NULL,   editable = FALSE,   index = NULL,   limit = NULL,   use_arrow = FALSE,   width = NULL,   height = NULL,   elementId = NULL )

title: Create a Perspective Interactive Viewer — perspective
text: data data.frame matrix display. columns Character vector column names show. NULL, columns shown. group_by Character vector column names group rows (row pivots). split_by Character vector column names split columns (column pivots). sort list two-element vectors, containing column name direction ("asc", "desc", "col asc", "col desc", "asc abs", "desc abs", "col asc abs", "col desc abs"). example: list(c("mpg", "desc")). filter list three-element vectors, containing column name, operator ("==", "!=", ">", "<", ">=", "<=", "begins ", "contains", "ends ", "", "", "null", "null"), value. example: list(c("cyl", "==", "6")). filter_op Character string controlling multiple filters combined: "" (default) "". NULL, Perspective default ("") used. expressions Character vector Perspective expression strings computed columns. example: c('"Profit" / "Sales"'). aggregates named list mapping column names aggregate functions. example: list(mpg = "avg", hp = "sum"). plugin Character string specifying visualization plugin. Options include: "Datagrid", "Y Bar", "X Bar", "Y Line", "X/Y Line", "Y Area", "Y Scatter", "XY Scatter", "Treemap", "Sunburst", "Heatmap". plugin_config list plugin-specific configuration options. theme Character string specifying CSS theme. Options: "Pro Light", "Pro Dark", "Monokai", "Solarized Light", "Solarized Dark", "Vaporwave", "Dracula", "Gruvbox", "Gruvbox Dark". Default "Pro Light". settings Logical; whether show settings/configuration panel sidebar. Default TRUE. interactive UI users drag--drop columns, change chart types, add filters, etc. title Character string viewer title. NULL, title shown. editable Logical; whether data grid user-editable. Default FALSE. index Character string naming column use table's primary key. set, psp_update() performs upserts (matching rows updated instead appended) psp_remove() can delete rows key. Must name column present data. Default NULL (index). limit Single positive integer specifying maximum number rows table hold. new rows added beyond limit, oldest rows removed (rolling window). Mutually exclusive index. Default NULL (limit). use_arrow Logical; TRUE, serialize data using Arrow IPC format (base64-encoded) better performance large datasets. Requires arrow package. Default FALSE. width Widget width (CSS string numeric pixels). height Widget height (CSS string numeric pixels). elementId Optional explicit element ID widget.

title: perspectiveR 0.3.1
text: Fixed theme initialization: themes now apply atomically plugin via restore(), preventing flash default colors first render. Added pkgdown site interactive article. Resized logo.

title: perspectiveR 0.3.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-03-30 Added psp_schema(), psp_size(), psp_columns(), psp_validate_expressions() proxy functions table introspection. Added filter_op parameter programmatic filter operators. Added limit parameter cap number rows loaded table. Added expressions parameter computed/virtual columns. Added windowed export support psp_export() via start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col parameters. Added three new demo apps: streaming stock market, editable table, expression builder.

title: perspectiveR 0.2.0
text: Added index parameter keyed/indexed tables. Added psp_remove() delete rows primary key. Added psp_export() export view data JSON, CSV, columns, Arrow. Added psp_save() retrieve current viewer configuration. Added psp_on_update() subscribe table update events. Added input$<outputId>_select event row/data-point selection. Added theme support dark mode custom styling.

title: perspectiveR 0.1.0
text: Initial release. perspective() widget support multiple chart types. Shiny integration via perspectiveOutput(), renderPerspective(), perspectiveProxy(). Proxy functions: psp_update(), psp_replace(), psp_clear(), psp_restore(), psp_reset(). Arrow IPC serialization high-performance data transfer. Bundled Shiny demo app run_example().
